tags.gist: Says the paper omits GenAI functions that output a physical patient-specific implant, where scoping to the GenAI component ignores the riskiest handoff.
Argues the category is foreseeable and asks CDRH to connect this paper with its point-of-care 3D printing production-system concept.
Suggests a physical-output modifier placing implant-geometry functions presumptively at the high-consequence end, since surgeons cannot see internal properties.
Supports evaluating the final configured device, but for physical outputs would make the validated production system, with a generative design envelope, the unit of evaluation.
Wants clinical confirmation for implant-generating functions to include physical testing such as dimensional and worst-case mechanical evidence, not only clinician adjudication.
Says accepting more premarket uncertainty is not appropriate for functions producing permanent implants, since monitoring cannot remediate without surgery.
Would add printer, material and postprocessing changes, and their combinations, as re-benchmarking triggers, with tiered handling that a PCCP could enumerate.
Wants production systems to pin model versions so no upstream update can change geometry without passing a release gate.
Recommends a two-signature release, surgeon plus manufacturer release authority, keeping accountability with the manufacturer while bounding the clinician's role.
Says a design function writing a build file takes an irreversible action, so human-oversight checkpoints should be required, not optional, for physical outputs.
Wants a proportionate digital record for each implant that adds the identity of model and configuration and whether geometry was generated or edited.
Summarizes: make physical output and reversibility an explicit risk dimension, with implant geometry presumptively high consequence.
Summarizes: premarket evaluation should cover the validated production system, with a prospectively defined envelope and physical evidence of conformance.
Summarizes: do not extend reliance on postmarket monitoring to functions that produce permanent implants.
Summarizes: couple change control across model, firmware, build, material and postprocessing changes, using tiered triggers and version pinning.
Summarizes: surgeon approval and manufacturing release as separate gates, plus a record tying each implant's configuration to its outcome.
